tagline.text: A headland at the western tip of Maricaban Island for wall diving and snorkeling

location.label: Location
location.text: Western tip of Maricaban Island, Tingloy, Batangas (reached by boat from Anilao)

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: December–April dry season (November–February is relatively cool)

duration.label: Time needed
duration.text: Day trip to 2 days and 1 night

children.text: Sepoc Point is a small headland and beach at the western tip of Maricaban Island in Tingloy, known for its coral gardens and a vertical-wall dive site. Eagle Point Resort manages it, so only resort guests and tour bookers can enter, and the usual way to get there is by boat from Anilao.

Sepoc Point is a headland at the western tip of Maricaban Island in Tingloy, the only island municipality in Batangas. It lies on the Verde Island Passage side where Batangas Bay and Balayan Bay meet, and it combines a wide sandy beach, a rocky shore and a small pocket of sand beside the point. A small hill separates the beach from the rest of the island, and a rocky cliff on top serves as a viewpoint. Depending on the guide, it is also called Sepoc Island or Sepoc Beach.

The main reason to come is the sea. A coral garden extends in front of the beach, making for good snorkeling, and on the west side of the beach is a dive site called Sepoc Wall. Dive-site directories describe a vertical wall from 5 m to about 28 m covered in soft corals, with leaf fish, anemonefish, frogfish and lionfish. Nearby Mapating Rock is also mentioned as a popular dive site, and Eagle Point can arrange dive tours.

The beach is owned and managed by Eagle Point Resort. A guide updated in late 2024 says access is limited to resort guests and people who book the "Sepoc Beach Tour." So this is not a beach you simply turn up at; you book boat and entry through the resort. Tour prices and rules can change, so check before you book. Even for resort guests, beach access hours, group size and whether the entrance fee applies may differ, so ask at check-in. The entrance fee is split into adult and child rates, and children aged 6 and under are reportedly free.

It is close to Anilao pier, so a day trip from Manila is possible, but travel alone takes 3–4 hours. One trip report describes catching a morning bus from Manila, boarding a boat around noon and returning after the sunset at Eagle Point, and calls the schedule very tight. If you want to relax, stay a night in Anilao.

A vertical wall west of the beach, covered in soft corals from 5 m to about 28 m. One report calls it one of Batangas' best sites, while another says even beginners can reach it. Accounts differ, so check the current and the required level with a dive shop.
A coral reef garden is said to lie just a few meters off the sandy beach. Guides advise wearing aqua shoes because of sharp reef and coral, and not stepping on the coral.
Climbing the small hill takes about
15 minutes
, and the rocky cliff at the top is said to look down on two islands. The view is good before sunset, but wear non-slip shoes.
The beach has a covered pavilion, toilets and showers. A large bungalow sells drinks only, and there is no restaurant or shop.
Many visitors also tour Sombrero Island, about
10 minutes
by boat from Sepoc. A 2024 guide advises visiting Sombrero first, because landing on the island can be difficult in waves.
The western coast near Anilao and Eagle Point is described as good for sunsets. After the tour, some people rest near the resort restaurant and watch the sun go down.
Eagle Point has Terrace Hotel rooms and cottages, and a 2024 guide lists nightly rates in the range of about
. Rates depend on room type and date, so confirm when you book.
Some itineraries combine Tingloy's other beaches, Masasa Beach and Mang Oscar's Beach. This must be arranged in advance with the resort and boat, and costs extra.

Take SLEX and the STAR Tollway, exit at Batangas City and find Eagle Point with a navigation app; parking is listed as free.
The resort's private transfer is listed at about

The 2024 guide recommends December to April as the dry season and says weekends and holidays are crowded. March–May is said to be the hottest, so for cooler weather choose November–February.
When waves are high, the boat ride is longer and landing on Sombrero Island is difficult. One report says the east side had big waves, so they snorkeled at a calmer spot on the west.
Diving is generally best in the dry season when water conditions and visibility are good, but actual current and visibility vary day to day, so check with a dive shop.
Around New Year, Holy Week, weekends and holidays, visitor numbers surge and the boats and beach can be crowded. If you want a quieter atmosphere, book on a weekday.

and may vary depending on local conditions.
Sepoc Beach has no restaurant or shop, only a pavilion, toilets and showers. Lunch can be arranged in advance through Eagle Point as a set menu (about
per person). It is described as grilled meat or fish with rice, pancit canton, fruit and iced tea. Outside food and drinks are restricted, but drinking water and snacks are reportedly allowed.

The standard place to stay is the Terrace Hotel rooms or cottages at Eagle Point Resort. At the resort restaurant, Eagle's Nest, you can order à la carte, and buffets run mainly on weekends with at least 100 guests, starting from about
per person. Camping or pitching tents at Sepoc Beach is not allowed. Pets are also not allowed on the beach or in the resort grounds.
Book the tour through Eagle Point Resort. Once your date is set, arrange the boat and lunch together.
The boat rocks with the waves. If you are not a strong swimmer, swim only near the shore.
Wear aqua shoes because of sharp rocks and coral, and do not step on coral while snorkeling.
Mobile signal on both Smart and Globe can be patchy, so confirm your schedule in advance.
Use sunscreen free of oxybenzone, benzophenone and parabens, and bring a reusable water bottle.
Carry out all your trash. A crow can snatch snacks, so keep food covered.
If you plan to dive, check your certification, insurance and equipment with the dive shop in advance.
Visiting Sombrero Island first increases the chance of landing.
Fitting Sepoc, Sombrero and sunset into a single day makes the schedule very tight. One trip report also said time ran short trying to do everything, so decide your priorities.
Watch your belongings. Leave bags and shoes in a visible place on the beach and keep valuables at the resort.
Sepoc Beach is not a public beach but resort property. Only guests and tour bookers can enter, and unauthorized access is not allowed.
When waves are high, the boat ride gets longer and landing on Sombrero Island may be impossible.
Coral and reef are sharp. Wear shoes so you do not get hurt, and do not touch the coral.
Camping and pets are not allowed on the beach.
Prices differed greatly even between 2019 and 2024. Check the latest rates before booking.
In an emergency, the unified Tingloy emergency number is 911.
A small island about
10 minutes
by boat from Sepoc. Landing can be difficult in waves, and the sea on the west side is said to be good for snorkeling.
A white-sand beach in Tingloy, said to be good for sunsets. Adding it to the Sepoc tour costs extra for the boat.
The dive town on the way to Sepoc. Resorts and dive shops are clustered there.
A ridge hike near Anilao; from the summit you can see Maricaban Island and Sombrero Island. Many people add it as a next-day plan.
